transcript: Mia Farrow and Patti LuPone are back on Broadway in a two hander comedy called The Roommate by Jen Silverman. In the play, Patti's character Robyn has just moved from New York to rural Iowa to live with Mia's character Sharon. Both women are somewhat looking for new beginnings and over the course of a few months or so, to get to know each other and learn more about themselves in the process. It’s a simple premise but a great vehicle for Mia and Patti who I thought had wonderful chemistry and made great comedy of their contrasting characters. Sharon is a little awkward and insecure whereas Robyn is blunt and assured. The ways that they interact with and surprise each other is the main source of humor in this piece, which at about 90 minutes with no intermission, smartly avoids overstaying its welcome. With that, other playbill for my collection.
